speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) how much casino entry fees have been collected from Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents since the fees were introduced; (b) how effective have the entry fees been in deterring problem gambling; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider doing away with the annual entry fee to further discourage compulsive gamblers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Annual entry levy holders tend to have higher incomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For these affluent individuals who want to visit the casinos more often, such as Premium Players, the annual entry levy provides convenience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Keep in mind that the levies are not our only measure of deterrence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have also put in place social safeguards targeting individuals who are at risk of problem gambling.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Frequent visitors to the casinos are identified by the National Council on Problem Gambling.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: With regard to the annual entry fee, I know that the Second Minister had said that most of those who are on this entry permit tend to be from higher-income groups.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, if it is a problem of problem gambling, then the factor of income should not come into play.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Problem gambling, regardless of your background or your income level, should still be combated, which is why I continue to make the call to do away with the annual entry fee.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Because if we acknowledge that problem gambling plagues people from all backgrounds, then having a higher disposable income should not be a criterion to keep entry permit on an annualised basis.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, some of our social safeguards go beyond that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are visit limits, for example, and we can even impose an exclusion order.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, it is not a matter of paying the levy and then being able to enter the casinos.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is also a follow-up question relating to social safeguards and I believe that the Minister for Social and Family Development will be addressing it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I think we should let him share with us.
